solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What's provided in iron pipe?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the condition word within the metal symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what an iron pipe might supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is only a link; the clue reads as a question about plumbing, but 'pipe' is the musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute, a type of pipe played in military bands.

clue.text: Trick in board game gets the bird

parts.note: flam is an old word for a trick or deception
taken as written
Go is the Japanese board game of stones

explanation.surface: Cheating in a board game earns the player a jeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being booed, but 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a pink wading bird with long legs.

clue.text: Pay for power at hotel? Here's a way

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
taken as written
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Covering a hotel's power costs, offered as a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a path for walkers, a way across country or beside a road.

clue.text: Plastered on vacation, so I'm in AA, getting sorted out for this?

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the collected letters are rearranged
a word on vacation has been emptied of its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written: Alcoholics Anonymous

explanation.surface: A drunk holidaymaker confesses to joining Alcoholics Anonymous to get their drinking problem sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Plastered to PD; 'getting sorted out' rearranges PD SO IM IN AA. The definition is just 'this', pointing back at the whole drunken scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is an uncontrollable craving for alcohol, the condition that sends someone plastered to AA.

clue.text: Angry couple, not married, laying siege to artist

indicators.note: besiegers surround a place, so these letters go round the other
not here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an item is a romantically linked couple
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An unmarried pair furiously besieging a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the married letter, leaving ITE, which 'laying siege to' wraps around the Academician. 'couple' as a romantic pair is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a straight synonym of furious or angry.

clue.text: Single idiot interrupting my serious mood

parts.note: sole means single, only one

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a nit is an idiot

explanation.surface: A lone fool butting in on someone's grave frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemnity is gravity and seriousness of manner, the serious mood of a formal occasion.

clue.text: Cosmic order, endlessly renewed, framing new moment of time

indicators.note: framing means surrounding like a picture frame, so the letters go around the other piece
renewed means made over afresh, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The universe's order, being forever remade, enclosing something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter to give ORDE; 'renewed' rearranges that with the first word, and 'framing' wraps the result around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A microsecond is a millionth of a second, a tiny instant.

clue.text: Fool about, elevating line in verse

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevating means lifting up, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so this letter goes within the poem

parts.note: an ode is a verse

explanation.surface: Messing around while lifting a line of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives ON, which 'elevating' turns into NO; 'Fool about' looks like a phrasal verb but 'Fool' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a silly person, a fool.

clue.text: Idiot's houses and French property

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so this piece contains the other

parts.note: an idiot is an ass, and the possessive adds S
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A fool's homes and holdings in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun, but it is the containment verb, putting the French word inside the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value that someone owns, such as land or goods.

clue.text: Way of working to fill a second book

indicators.note: to fill means to go inside, so this piece is placed within the other letters

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A method of working that takes up a second volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Wrong to collapse, hanging on with most of soccer team sent off

parts.note: to collapse is to fall

indicators.note: sent off means removed from the field, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: hanging on means holding firm, tenacious
a soccer team has eleven players, so most of it is ten

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a side collapsing while clinging on after nearly all its players are dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent off' removes TEN (most of an eleven-man team) from TENACIOUS, leaving ACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallacious means based on a mistaken belief or faulty reasoning, so it is a synonym for wrong.

clue.text: I refuse to accept the modern deadlock

parts.words: I refuse to accept the modern
parts.note: someone who rejects modern ways describes themself as out of date, a phrase of a pronoun with a verb and a French-derived adjective

explanation.surface: A stubborn old-timer's declaration that they reject modern things, then a standoff.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 1'1,5 the answer reads I'M PASSÉ: whoever refuses modern things is old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a stalemate between two sides.

clue.text: Offend boxing squad, English and European, coming to train

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so the letters go round the others

parts.note: to sin is to offend
a team is a squad

explanation.surface: Insulting a boxing team of English and European fighters who arrive to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but is the containment signal; 'train' is a noun, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam engine is a locomotive, the engine that pulls a train, and loosely the train itself.

clue.text: Low source of luminance one found in extremes of night — like this?

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so these letters go within the outer pair
extremes are the two end letters of the word
a source is where something starts, so take the first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A faint glow in the dark of night, lit by one dim source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is a verb, the sound of cattle, not a measure of brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlit describes a night scene lit only by the moon's weak light, the picture the clue paints.

clue.text: Neglected child, say, returning to snatch absolute bargain

indicators.note: to snatch means to grab and hold, so the reversed pair holds the other letters
returning means coming back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: say is a signal for an example, eg
absolute means utter, complete
a snip is a bargain

explanation.surface: A street child coming back to grab a real bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives EG, reversed to GE by 'returning', which holds UTTER SNIP. 'say' looks like a verb but is the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a ragged, neglected child of the slums, one who grows up on the street.

clue.text: Limits of seriousness to marine weather event

parts.note: the limits of the word are its outer letters, S and S, written out in full
RM is the Royal Marines, so a marine

explanation.surface: Taking seriousness to the limit for a weather report at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The limits are the first and last S, so the leaf spells them out with the joining word written in.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert storm whipping up blowing grains is a weather event of strong wind.

clue.text: Tuesday's gathering wind up after time for Guardian's business

indicators.note: gathering means collecting up into itself, so the day encloses the rest

parts.note: Tue is the abbreviation for Tuesday, and 's means has

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so this piece follows the time letter
in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gale is a wind

explanation.surface: A Tuesday meeting being wound up after hours for a newspaper's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like ending a meeting, but GALE is turned to ELAG by 'up'. 'Guardian' is not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guardianship and protection, the role or work of a guardian or tutor.

clue.text: Swedish physicist's deep uncertainty over computer storage

definitions.note: the 's here reads as 'is', so this is the scientist's name

parts.note: angst is deep anxiety
ROM is read-only memory

explanation.surface: A Swedish scientist's anxiety about computer memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places ANGST above ROM in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was the 19th-century Swedish physicist after whom the unit of length is named.

clue.text: Lots to spend for toasted bread?

definitions.meaning: a surplus of cash that can be spent freely
bread is slang for cash, and to toast bread is to burn it a little

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: bread is money, and toasting is burning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having cash in such quantity that one can waste it is the idiom's meaning, so it fits lots to spend.

clue.text: A litre, in leak, gets out

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: to seep is to leak

explanation.surface: A litre escaping through a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'gets out', but alone it means unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is out, dead to the world.

clue.text: Wild animal's mother rising on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A wild animal mother climbing up on top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes reckless, impulsive behaviour, so it is a synonym for wild.

clue.text: Gratitude expressed during functions in Surrey town

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function, so functions gives sines
ta is an informal British word of thanks

explanation.surface: Thanks given at events in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for 'thank you'. Staines is a town on the Thames west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines, now Staines-upon-Thames, is a town in the county of Surrey near Heathrow.

clue.text: Talk with a daughter that's ahead of fashion?

indicators.note: ahead of means placed before, so these letters come first in the sequence

parts.note: to dress is to fashion or style

explanation.surface: A chat with a daughter who is ahead of the trends.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech, so it is a talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Protective clothing in operation after a month

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so this piece follows the month

parts.note: Apr is the abbreviation for April
on means working, in operation

explanation.surface: Wearing protective clothing for surgery a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' suggests surgery, but 'in operation' simply means switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is tied over clothes to protect them, as in a kitchen or workshop.

clue.text: Review in English very much leading to anger where the writer works

indicators.note: leading to means coming before, so the earlier pieces precede the last one
in means placed inside, so this piece goes within the intensifier

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so kind'
a crit is a critical review
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A critique in English that leads to fury in a writing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the review inside the intensifier; 'leading to' sets everything before the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, the piece of furniture at which a writer sits to work.

clue.text: Origin of hippie melody?

indicators.note: the origin is where a word starts, so take its first letter

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: Where did hippie music come from?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the 1960s rock musical of this name, a key source of hippie-era songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical Hair was a product of the hippie counterculture and launched many of its songs.

clue.text: Sweet style captured by pen-tip at work

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the hairstyle goes into the other letters
at work means being worked on, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: a perm is a hair style

explanation.surface: A style of writing caught by a pen nib as it works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges the nib letters to PEPINT, and 'captured by' puts the hairdo inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint is a mint-flavoured sweet, a sugary confection.

clue.text: Instructive period crucial to betterment

indicators.note: crucial means central, so the letters at the heart of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A stretch of teaching that is essential for self-improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university year is divided into terms, periods of instruction.
